Profit-oriented services will tend to locate in or near market concentrations. This characteristic will tend to increase the intensity of economic impacts on the towns of Hardin and Sheridan.
Even though the business community responds relatively rapidly to a rising demand, a significant lag between demonstrated needs and reasonable fulfillment cannot be avoided, particularly in the smaller communities. Major concerns of an expanding community always include the adequacy of electrical power and natural gas supplies as well as communication systems. Present basic systems for all three are adequate to handle any projected development. However, there will be a need for considerable expansion in local services in some direct proportion to the increase in population.
Coal Related Industries Impacts
The proposed Sarpy Creek mine would create a need for a number of services provided by related industries: maintenance, repair parts, and consumables such as fuel and explosives. Maintenance businesses will provide tires, rubber belting, welding and other services. New items of equipment will arrive by rail, as will supplies such as reels of cable for draglines, fuel for equipment and ammonium nitrate for blasting. Telecommunications and radio facilities will be needed. Westmoreland may need expanded insurance, legal, and banking services. Consulting and engineering firms may be needed for environmental studies and new construction.
There are no related industries near the existing Sarpy Creek mine. Some services might come from Hardin, but most would probably come from Billings, as this city is a major service center for eastern Montana.
